newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Troops defending mortar positions repulsed counter-attack by Tamil rebels (LTTE) on Tuesday night, Sixty four servicemen, including four officers, and over 150 separatists killed in the attack.
Twenty LTTE suspects waiting to board an Airlanka flight to the west taken into custody at Bandaranaike International Airport and handed over to the CID, police said.
More than 150 LTTE rebels and 64 soldiers killed during a six-hour battle at Periyamadu, north of government held town of Vavuniya, on Tuesday.

Main opposition United National Party (UNP) leader Ranil Wickremesinghe asks party member Sarath Kongahage to discipline himself. Investigations show that Kongahage had been the architect of a move to bring an impeachment motion against President Kumaratunga, UNP sources said.
The two main accused in the killing of former ruling People's Alliance coaltion member Nalanda Ellawala refused bail. Ellawala was gunned down in Ratnapura in central Sri Lanka earlier this year.

UNP's Sarath Kongahage says his party has "thorwn him to the wolves" in accusing him of planning an impeachment motion against the president and trying to form another party. Kongahage was recently warned by UNP leader Wickremesinghe to discipline himself.
Government to conduct survey to assess how many children of school going age do not attend school.
